findings.title: Saved-all feedback in generator desyncs from actual bank state (dedup silently drops re-saves)
findings.problem: save(_:) calls bank.add(...) (whose @discardableResult Bool reports whether it was actually inserted) but ignores the return value and unconditionally marks the question Saved via savedIDs.insert. WorkbookQuestionBankStore.add dedups by lowercased prompt+answer, so if the generator produces a question whose prompt+answer already exists in the bank (very common when regenerating with the same source/instructions), add() returns false and nothing is stored, yet the card flips to '已保存 · Saved' and the Save button disables. The learner believes a question was saved into the bank when it was not. Same applies to 'Save all'.
findings.fix: Capture the boolean: let didInsert = bank.add(...). Only insert into savedIDs when didInsert is true, or (better) treat an existing duplicate as already-saved by marking it Saved while surfacing nothing misleading. Mirror the grading view's isInBank() content-match approach so the Saved badge reflects bank membership, not just a tap.

findings.title: Generator 'Saved' state is keyed on GeneratedReviewQuestion.id which is regenerated each decode, so it cannot survive a Regenerate and is purely per-render UUID
findings.problem: GeneratedReviewQuestion.id is `let id = UUID()` assigned at decode time (AIWordExplanationService.swift:1376). On Regenerate, generate() replaces `generated` and clears savedIDs/revealed, which is correct. However there is no persistence of which generated items were already added to the bank across a regenerate; combined with the dedup-driven add described above, a learner who saves a question, regenerates, and gets a textually identical question will see it as un-saved and tapping Save is a silent no-op (add() returns false). This compounds finding #1's confusion.
findings.fix: After loading bank, pre-populate savedIDs for any freshly generated question whose dedup key already exists in bank.questions (e.g. via bank.contains(WorkbookQuestion(generated: q))), so already-banked items render as Saved and the Save button correctly reflects reality.

findings.title: Detail view 'Add all to Review Bank' gives no partial-success feedback and re-tap is impossible after first add
findings.problem: The button loops `for question in session.questions { _ = bank.add(question) }` discarding each Bool, then sets addedAll = true and disables itself permanently for the lifetime of the view. If some questions were already in the bank (e.g. they were added from the live grading screen via 'Add to Bank'), the button still claims '已加入题库 · Added to Bank' even though it may have added zero new items. It also cannot reflect bank membership when the detail is first opened (always shows the un-added label even if everything is already banked), which is inconsistent with the live grading screen that uses content-based isInBank().
findings.fix: Initialize addedAll by checking bank membership on appear (e.g. session.questions.allSatisfy { bank.contains($0) }), and/or count actual insertions from add()'s return to show 'Added N' vs already present. Keep the button enabled when not all questions are banked.

findings.title: Redundant local rebinding of imageID inside .task(id:) is dead code (harmless but misleading)
findings.problem: Inside `.task(id: imageID)` the closure does `let id = imageID` then uses `id`. The comment-implied intent (snapshotting to avoid capturing self/changing state) is unnecessary: imageID is a `let` stored property of a value-type view, already immutable and safely captured. The local alias adds noise and can mislead a future reader into thinking there is a capture hazard being defended against. The async load itself is correct: file IO runs in Task.detached off the main actor and the resulting value-type Image is assigned back on the MainActor-isolated view, which is sound.
findings.fix: Remove the `let id = imageID` line and use imageID directly, or leave as-is; this is style-only with no runtime effect.

findings.title: Re-tapping Grade double-counts stats and duplicates history sessions + on-disk images
findings.location: grade() lines 571-619; canGrade lines 65-67; gradeButton line 373
findings.problem: After a successful grade, `isGrading` returns to false while `workbookImages`/`answerImages` remain populated, so `canGrade` is true and the Grade button is re-enabled. Each subsequent tap of Grade unconditionally: (1) calls `LearningActivityStore.shared.recordQuestionsGraded(graded.questions.count)`, inflating today's questionsGraded streak/stat by the full count again; (2) calls `WorkbookGradingHistoryStore.shared.add(session)`, which inserts without any dedup (WorkbookBank.swift add() lines 318-321), producing duplicate history entries for the same workbook; and (3) re-runs `WorkbookImageStore.saveAll(...)` which writes a fresh copy of every scanned photo to Application Support under new UUIDs. So grading the same images twice triple-pollutes: stats, history list, and disk usage. The most likely real-world trigger is a user who re-grades after tweaking custom instructions, or who taps Grade again to 'retry' — all of which the UI permits. None of this existed in HEAD (recordQuestionsGraded, history persistence and image save are all new this session).
findings.fix: Make re-grade idempotent or block it. Options: track a per-input signature (e.g. hash of wbImages+ansImages+custom) and skip session/stat/image persistence when it matches the last graded signature; or reset inputs after a successful grade; or gate the persistence block behind a `!didSaveSession || inputsChanged` check. At minimum, only call recordQuestionsGraded / history.add / saveAll once per distinct input set. Clearing `didSaveSession` and re-counting on every tap is the core defect.

findings.title: Camera capture downscales a full-resolution photo synchronously on the main actor
findings.problem: CameraImagePicker delivers `info[.originalImage]` (the full-resolution camera frame, often 12MP / several MB) as JPEG via its delegate, which fires on the main thread. The `.fullScreenCover` onCapture closure calls `addCapturedImage`, which runs `downscaledJPEG(data)` — a synchronous CGImageSource thumbnail + JPEG re-encode — directly on the MainActor before appending. Every other ingestion path (Photos via `loadDownscaled`, Files via `loadDownscaledFiles`, drag-drop via the Task in handleDrop) performs the same downscale OFF the main actor in an async/static context. So the camera path uniquely blocks the UI for the duration of the decode/encode (tens of ms+, larger on older devices), and does it while the full-screen cover is dismissing — a visible hitch.
findings.fix: Move the downscale off the main actor for the camera path too, mirroring the other ingestion methods. E.g. make addCapturedImage async/Task-based: `Task { let processed = await Task.detached { downscaledJPEG(data) }.value; await MainActor.run { append } }`, or route camera bytes through the same `loadDownscaled`-style off-main helper.

findings.title: "Add to Bank" button reports success even when nothing was added (empty-key questions)
findings.location: addToBank lines 629-632; addAllToBank lines 634-640; isInBank lines 625-627
findings.problem: `bank.add(...)` returns false and stores nothing when the dedup key is empty — and the key is `question + "∣" + correctAnswer` lowercased/trimmed (WorkbookBank.swift dedupKey lines 228-232, guarded in add() line 185). A graded question whose `question` and `correctAnswer` are both empty (tolerant decode defaults them to "") therefore never enters the bank. But addToBank ignores the return value (`_ = bank.add(...)`) and unconditionally does `savedToBankIDs.insert(question.id)`, so isInBank() then returns true and the card shows '已在题库 · In Bank' (disabled). The user is told the question was banked when it silently wasn't, and it will be absent from WorkbookQuestionBankView. Low impact because such fully-empty questions are rare, but the UI state is dishonest.
findings.fix: Only mark as banked when the add (or pre-existing membership) is real: `if bank.add(WorkbookQuestion(graded: question)) || bank.containsGraded(question) { savedToBankIDs.insert(question.id) }`. Apply the same in addAllToBank so the bulk button doesn't mark un-addable questions as in-bank.

findings.title: "Add all to Review Bank" bulk button gives no added-state feedback and stays active
findings.location: resultsSection bulk button lines 442-450; addAllToBank lines 634-640
findings.problem: Unlike the per-question card (which flips to '已在题库' and disables) and unlike the analogous GradedSessionDetailView.addToBankButton (which tracks `addedAll` and disables), the '全部加入题库 · Add all to Review Bank' button here never reflects that it was pressed and never disables. Repeated taps are safe due to bank dedup, but the user gets no confirmation the action took effect, which is inconsistent with the rest of the feature's UX and may prompt repeated tapping. Not data loss, purely a state/feedback gap.
findings.fix: Add an `@State private var didAddAllToBank = false`, set it in addAllToBank(), and reflect it on the label/disabled state (e.g. show '已全部加入 · Added all' and `.disabled(didAddAllToBank)`), resetting it alongside savedToBankIDs at the start of grade().

findings.title: Re-grading the same loaded photos creates a duplicate session, re-saves the images to disk, and double-counts questionsGraded
findings.problem: After a successful grade(), `isGrading` is reset to false but `workbookImages`/`answerImages` are NOT cleared, so `canGrade` becomes true again and the Grade button is re-enabled while the same photos are still loaded. Tapping Grade a second time runs the full path again: WorkbookImageStore.saveAll() writes a SECOND copy of the identical scans to Application Support under fresh UUIDs, WorkbookGradingHistoryStore.shared.add() inserts a SECOND GradedSession for the same workbook, and LearningActivityStore.shared.recordQuestionsGraded(graded.questions.count) is called again — inflating today's questionsGraded (and thus activityScore/heatmap) by the question count on every extra tap. Unlike the review-bank add() which dedups on prompt+answer, GradedSession.add() and recordQuestionsGraded() have no idempotency guard. This is a regression introduced by wiring the new persistence (image store + history + activity counter) into a button that stays live after the first run.
